subject.title: [Feature]: Include interaction metadata in Discord button callbacks

question: Should generic Discord component clicks expose a new agent-visible structured interaction metadata envelope, and which fields are safe public agent context versus plugin-only callback data?
rationale: This changes the public agent inbound context and exposes Discord message, user, and callback identifiers, so maintainers need to choose the schema and trust boundary before implementation.

options.title: Add Typed Agent Metadata
options.body: Expose a narrow documented envelope with original message id, interaction kind, component id/custom data, label/value details, and clicker identity, backed by Discord plugin tests.

options.title: Keep Metadata Plugin-Only
options.body: Leave rich interaction fields only in plugin interactive handlers and document that stateful Discord workflows should use plugin callbacks rather than generic agent fallback messages.

options.title: Start With Sender And Message IDs
options.body: Expose only clicker and originating message ids first, deferring callback payload semantics until a broader inbound metadata contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Add Typed Agent Metadata
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow documented envelope with original message id, interaction kind, component id/custom data, label/value details, and clicker identity, backed by Discord plugin tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Discord component callback boundary and plugin-interactive metadata path are most strongly tied to this person's recent commits.
